review_notes:
I read the whole file, lines 1–139. I did not open any related sources, because the file's own text was enough to judge the candidates. There are two pairs of near-duplicate proofs.

1. `pairing_mul_left` and `pairing_mul_right` are each a two-line `simp only` followed by `finprod_mul_distrib`. The real shared work, finite support of the local factors, is already factored into `pairing_hasFiniteMulSupport`. Another helper would be a thin wrapper around existing API and would save almost nothing.

2. `pairing_mulSingle_left` and `pairing_mulSingle_right` have the same shape of about seven lines. Each applies `pairing_eq_prod` with `s := {i}`, then runs `simp`, then closes the off-diagonal case with `mulSingle_eq_of_ne`. The off-diagonal branch differs in the side of the pairing and in which family is used. Sharing it would mean abstracting over the side, and that would need a swapped-argument pairing or a general helper. The result would likely be longer than the two short proofs it replaces. The duplication is routine unfolding plus a small branch, which the rubric treats as insufficient.

Beyond these two pairs I found no nontrivial repeated reasoning. The remaining declarations are one-line bundlings.

I did not test any proposed refactor, since I can't run Lean. My judgment that the mulSingle pair is too small to justify a helper rests on reading the proofs, not on measurement.
